title: Gabber's affine comparison for a henselian pair
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $z:Z\to X$ the closed immersion. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]
$$
z^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow H^q(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}F)
$$
is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$ ($H^q$ etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $z^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]). Only the pair form is asserted: for an affine scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in place of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the comparison with the closed fibre is false (see the report of lemma-weil-pbc-injective-restriction-acyclicity and the Lean docstring of AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.bijective_cohomologyMap_of_henselianRing).

proof.text: For degree zero identify the range of Spec(A/I)→Spec A with V(I). Every finite cover p:X′→Spec A is proper; Stein connectedness gives the required nonempty connected intersections of irreducible closed subsets with p⁻¹(V(I)). Apply the abelian finite-cover connectedness criterion to obtain an isomorphism on global sections. The proved formula cohomologyMap_zero_eq_globalSectionsUpperStarMap and the canonical H.equiv₀/global-sections bijections conjugate it to the degree-zero cohomology bijection.

Fix $q>0$ and assume the comparison is bijective in every smaller degree, for every torsion sheaf. Choose a monomorphism $\iota:F\hookrightarrow F'$ of torsion sheaves and write $Q=\operatorname{coker}(\iota)$. The resulting short exact sequence $0\to F\to F'\to Q\to0$ and its inverse image along $z$ give a commutative diagram of long exact cohomology sequences on $X$ and $Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-second-variable], together with the already proved local cohomologyMap_comp_extClass and cohomologyMap_comp_mk₀ naturality identities; the restriction map for $F'$ and $Q$ in degree $q-1$ is an isomorphism by the induction hypothesis.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09ZI (59.82.7), proof: short exact sequence and comparison diagram

proof.text: For injectivity, let $\xi\in H^q(X_{\Et},F)$ with $z^*\xi=0$. The pair $(A,0)$ is henselian ($B/0B=B$ for every finite $A$-algebra $B$), so affine Gabber effacement [lemma-weil-pbc-gabber-effacement] applied to $(A,0)$ and the class $\xi$ gives a monomorphism of torsion sheaves $F\hookrightarrow F'$ whose image kills $\xi$ in $H^q(X_{\Et},F')$; let $Q$ be its cokernel. By exactness of the upper long exact sequence of the ladder [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-second-variable], together with the already proved local cohomologyMap_comp_extClass and cohomologyMap_comp_mk₀ naturality identities, $\xi=\delta(\eta)$ for some $\eta\in H^{q-1}(X_{\Et},Q)$. In the lower sequence, $\delta(z^*\eta)=z^*\xi=0$ (commutativity of the ladder), so $z^*\eta$ is the image of some $\alpha\in H^{q-1}(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}F')$; by the induction hypothesis (surjectivity in degree $q-1$ for the torsion sheaf $F'$) $\alpha=z^*\beta$ with $\beta\in H^{q-1}(X_{\Et},F')$, and then $z^*(\eta-\bar\beta)=0$ where $\bar\beta$ is the image of $\beta$ in $H^{q-1}(X_{\Et},Q)$ (commutativity again); by the induction hypothesis (injectivity in degree $q-1$ for $Q$) $\eta=\bar\beta$, hence $\xi=\delta(\eta)=\delta(\bar\beta)=0$ by exactness of the upper sequence. (Rewritten by the lead at the spot check, 2026-10-10: the delivered text ended with a garbled sentence; the argument is Stacks' proof of 09ZI.)

source.place: Theorem Tag 09ZI, proof: Injectivity for $\mathcal F$ (59.82.7)

proof.text: For surjectivity, let $\eta\in H^q(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}F)$. Apply the same effacement lemma to the class on $Z$ to obtain a monomorphism $F\hookrightarrow F'$ whose image of $\eta$ is zero, with cokernel $Q$. Exactness of the lower long exact sequence writes $\eta$ as the image of a class in $H^{q-1}(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}Q)$. By the induction isomorphism for $Q$, lift this class to $H^{q-1}(X_{\Et},Q)$; exactness of the upper sequence then produces a class in $H^q(X_{\Et},F)$ mapping to $\eta$. This proves surjectivity, and induction over all $q$ proves the comparison.
